speaker: Doctor
text: I need to understand the nature of these breathing episodes. Are the stridor and wheezing episodes triggered specifically by feeding or crying? REQUEST TEST: Chest_XRay

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest_X-ray findings show evidence of tracheal compression and a vascular ring suggestive of a double aortic arch.

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. I also have Exacerbation during crying, Exacerbation during feeding, Exacerbation with neck flexion, Relief with neck extension, Occasional vomiting post-feeding.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. Born full term with no complications during birth. Social history: First child in the family. Lives with both parents. No exposure to smoking or pets in the household.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, diarrhea, rash, or other respiratory symptoms such as cough. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand your concern, but we must rule out anatomical causes first; have the infants been choking on secretions during feeds? REQUEST TEST: Laryngoscopy: REQUEST IMAGES: Lateral_Neck_XRay

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Laryngoscopy shows compression of the larynx and trachea with no evidence of foreign body aspiration or secretions. Lateral_Neck_XRay confirms the presence of a vascular ring with associated tracheal and esophageal compression.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Vascular Ring (likely Right Double Aortic Arch or Pulmonary Artery Slings) causing tracheal and esophageal compression.
